audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer phases[N].side read 'Skill' while the content layer and the packet both read Katarina/Katarina/Katarina/Katarina/Diana/Katarina/Diana. The page gave two different answers to who wins Level 6.
audit.why: The spikes are real and sourced: Lunar Rush is 22s at rank 1 unless Crescent Strike has marked you, so levels 3-5 are Katarina's; Moonfall at 100s is an on-command pull that ends the Death Lotus channel, so level 6 is Diana's; Pale Cascade (15s down to 9s) plus her passive attack speed win the 2+ item brawl.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side -> Katarina, phases[4].side -> Diana, phases[5].side -> Katarina, phases[6].side -> Diana, with ratings moved to match and phases[4].why / phases[6].why rewritten in the same proposal because their verdict flipped. win[0..6] already holds these values on disk.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit. dosFull[1].d was tradeGood pasted under 'Blink to daggers, not targets', dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad pasted under 'Fight away from your steel'. Six fields called Diana 'his' or 'him'. dosFull[2].d invented a 'fifteen-second invitation' — Crescent Strike is 8s at rank 1, and the 22s number that matters belongs to Lunar Rush.
audit.why: Two interactions decide this matchup and both are in Riot's text. Lunar Rush has no cooldown against a Moonlight-afflicted target, so a dodged 900-range Crescent Strike turns her engage into a 22-second commitment. Moonfall draws in and slows at 475 range; Katarina's R is flagged channel-interruptible, so that pull cancels Death Lotus outright — which is exactly why level 6 belongs to her.
audit.corrected: Real numbers now in breakdown.cooldowns (E 22s->14s and free on Moonlight, R 100/90/80, W 15s->9s); the pull-cancels-channel rule stated in tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d and phases[4].why; every misgendered pronoun corrected.
